capitals.name: Qatif
capitals.note: The page names no single capital: the seat moved between Qatif and Awal, 'in 513 AH, the capital went back to Qatif', and after 531 AH between Qatif and al-Hasa. The years are the emirate's, the city is the one the page names most often.

correction.text: Bahrain (the Gulf coast of eastern Arabia), al-Hasa and Qatif with the Kuwait end, valid from 1077

keyframe_review.note: 73,498 km2 for 1072-1168, a coastal strip from Kuwait through Qatif and Qatar to the Emirates. Page: Abdullah bin Ali al-Uyuni 'defeated the Qarmatians in Bahrain and al-Hasa' in 1077-1078 and founded the dynasty (infobox 'Founded: 1076'); the shape starts five years early. The Uyunid page names Bahrain, al-Hasa, Qatif, Awal and Kuwait; it mentions neither the United Arab Emirates nor Oman, and the Cliopatria shape holds 119 cells of the UAE (43% of the 1072 shape) but only 15 of the 124 cells round Hofuf (al-Hasa). The corrected shape drops the UAE and adds a 100 km disc at Hofuf; Qatar (48 cells) and Kuwait (23) stay as Cliopatria draws them, unverified. The page gives no area figure.

correction.text: Bahrain, al-Hasa and Qatif as one Uyunid state; the page has it divided into two halves (al-Hasa and Qatif) in 531 AH (1136/37) and reunited in 587-605 AH (1191-1208/9), with no borders, so the shape is not split

keyframe_review.note: 73,692 km2 for 1169-1226. Page: the capital 'went back to Qatif' in 513 AH (1119/20); the page says 'In 531 AH ... his state was divided into two, one in al-Hasa and the other in Qatif' (1136/37) and 'Mohammed bin Abi al-Hussain united Qatif and Al-Hasa' in 587-605 AH (1191-1208/9). The halves are two lines of one dynasty with no borders on the page, so the dossier keeps one Uyunid state throughout (review fix: the first draft logged split and merge events against a 'principality of al-Hasa', which is not a state, while the keyframes still drew al-Hasa in the Uyunid shape). The Uyunid page names Bahrain, al-Hasa, Qatif, Awal and Kuwait; it mentions neither the United Arab Emirates nor Oman, and the Cliopatria shape holds 119 cells of the UAE (43% of the 1072 shape) but only 15 of the 124 cells round Hofuf (al-Hasa). The corrected shape drops the UAE and adds a 100 km disc at Hofuf; Qatar (48 cells) and Kuwait (23) stay as Cliopatria draws them, unverified. The page gives no area figure.

The Uyunid page names Bahrain, al-Hasa, Qatif, Awal and Kuwait; it mentions neither the United Arab Emirates nor Oman, and the Cliopatria shape holds 119 cells of the UAE (43% of the 1072 shape) but only 15 of the 124 cells round Hofuf (al-Hasa). keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1236-1252: Cliopatria ends the Uyunids in 1235, the year of the Salghurid invasion, but the Usfurids took Eastern Arabia only in 1253 ('in 1253 gained control of Eastern Arabia, including the islands of Bahrain'; Uyunid page: 'fell to the Usfurids of Banu Uqayl in 651 AH (1253 CE)'). The page does not say what the Salghurids kept; the shape is carried on unchanged and the Bahrain islands may have been held by Fars.

region.text: Bahrain and al-Hasa, taken from the Qarmatians

ledger.note: 1077: Abdullah bin Ali al-Uyuni defeats the Qarmatians and founds the Uyunid emirate. Page: 'In 1077-1078, an Arab sheikh named Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni defeated the Qarmatians in Bahrain and al-Hasa' with Seljuk help and 'founded the Uyunid dynasty'; infobox 'Founded: 1076'. The Qarmatians dossier dates the same event 1077 and the campaign from 1067.
1119: the Uyunid capital goes back to Qatif. Page: 'Then in 513 AH, the capital went back to Qatif' (513 AH is 1119/20; the page names no earlier capital).

region.text: Eastern Arabia including the islands of Bahrain

ledger.note: 1253: the Usfurids take Eastern Arabia and end the Uyunid emirate. Page: 'It then fell to the Usfurids of Banu Uqayl in 651 AH (1253 CE)'; Usfurids page: they 'in 1253 gained control of Eastern Arabia, including the islands of Bahrain' after Uyunid power was 'weakened by invasion in 1235 by the Salghurid Atabeg of Fars'. Cliopatria ends the Uyunids in 1235.

wars.name: Uyunid conquest of Bahrain and al-Hasa

certainty.note: The page gives places (Bahrain, al-Hasa, Qatif, Awal, Kuwait) and no boundary; the emirate was a string of oases and ports on the Gulf coast.

notes:
Pages: the Uyunid dynasty and the Usfurids (budget 1-2); both are short. The Uyunid page's infobox gives 'Founded: 1076' and 'Dissolution: 1253'; the text 1077-1078 and 651 AH (1253).
Cliopatria faults: the three shapes (1072-1235) start five years early, end 18 years early (the 1235 Salghurid invasion, which weakened but did not end the emirate) and run along the coast to the UAE, which no page supports; the corrected shape drops the UAE and adds al-Hasa round Hofuf. Qatar and Kuwait are kept unverified (the page names Kuwait, not Qatar).
AH dates are converted by the usual arithmetic and are good to a year: 513 AH = 1119/20, 531 AH = 1136/37, 587 AH = 1191/92, 605 AH = 1208/9. The two divisions (531 AH, 1136/37, and after 605 H, 1208/9) and the reunion (587-605 AH, 1191-1208/9) are told here and not in the ledger: the Uyunid page says 'his state was divided into two, one in al-Hasa and the other in Qatif', 'Mohammed bin Abi al-Hussain united Qatif and Al-Hasa' and 'The state was divided again after his assassination in 605 H', gives neither borders nor rulers for the halves, and the halves are lines of one dynasty, not states, so there are no split or merge events (review fix: the first draft logged them against a 'principality of al-Hasa'). The shape stays one Uyunid state, as Cliopatria draws it.
The page says the territory reached Najd and the Syrian desert 'under Muhammad b. Ahmad' (undated) and the Seljuk help of 1077-1078 is not described as vassalage; the Seljuk dossier may add an allegiance.
Counterparts without a dossier: usfurids (1253-1392, group me-09 or ia), the Salghurid Atabegs of Fars.
Gazetteer names needed: Awal (the island of Bahrain), Kuwait city region as a place, Hasa/al-Ahsa as a region.
Review repair (2026-10-20), page re-opened: the page lists no emirs with dates (it names Abdullah bin Ali al-Uyuni 1077-1078, his son al-Fadhl, Mohammed son of Al Fadhl I assassinated 531 AH, Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Abu'l-Hussin b. Abu Sinan, Mohammed bin Abi al-Hussain 587-605 AH and, in the infobox, Fadl III ibn Muhammad as the last), so identity.rulers stays empty. Undated extents on the page, not drawn: 'In his reign [al-Fadhl], the state extended to Kuwait' (Kuwait stays in the Cliopatria-derived shape) and 'Under Muhammad b. Ahmad ... the Uyunids' territory stretched from Najd to the Syrian desert'. The page has no sentence on the Salghurids or 1235; that comes from the Usfurids page. No counterpart dossier is needed for an al-Hasa branch.
